answer: Because the canyon count is verified against the wharf text itself, the ripple audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. Filling 173 aliases hence means producing 173 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 3 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
